title: Starter example pack · 7 sample cards (NOT the 700-card curriculum)

cards.question: Arkadaşım gelene kadar burada bekleyeceğim.
cards.answer: I'll wait here until my friend arrives.
cards.grammarHint: After until, use the present simple to refer to a future event.
vocabularyNotes: arrive = reach a place; arrive at school / arrive in Istanbul.

cards.question: You're at a café and you're ready to pay. Politely ask for the bill.
cards.answer: Could I have the bill, please?
vocabularyNotes: bill = a request for payment in a restaurant (UK/US); in US English, check is also common in restaurants.
bill can also mean a proposed law or a banknote, depending on context.

cards.question: You didn't know about yesterday's exam and didn't study enough. Imagine the opposite past situation. Use the third conditional.
cards.answer: If I had known about the exam, I would have studied harder.
cards.grammarHint: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

cards.question: Your classmate is confused by a problem. Reassure them that you will solve it together. Use 'figure out'.
vocabularyNotes: figure out = understand or solve something.
figure (noun) can also mean a number, a shape, or a person in a particular role.

cards.question: Friend: 'I haven't started the assignment yet.' Give friendly advice and mention that it is due tomorrow.
cards.answer: You should start soon. It's due tomorrow.
vocabularyNotes: due = expected or required by a particular time; due tomorrow = must be handed in tomorrow.
due to = because of (different meaning and structure).

cards.question: Compare theoretical knowledge and practical experience. Use the pattern 'There is a significant difference between ... and ...'.
cards.answer: There is a significant difference between theoretical knowledge and practical experience.
cards.grammarHint: There is a + adjective + difference between X and Y.
vocabularyNotes: significant = important or large enough to matter; a significant difference / significant impact.

cards.question: Explain that someone submitted the report yesterday, using the passive voice.
cards.grammarHint: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.
vocabularyNotes: submit = formally hand in work; submit an assignment / submit a report.
